projects.name: Partly
projects.summary: An Internal Family Systems (IFS)-based emotional wellness app for consumers, paired with a B2B web platform giving enterprise teams privacy-safe visibility into team emotional wellbeing.

overview.title: Understanding yourself, one part at a time
paragraphs: Partly applies Internal Family Systems framework to a self-guided app format. Users work through themed journeys built from 75+ short interactive lessons combining insight, reflection, journaling, and choice-making, plus a companion that remembers context across sessions. It's deliberately positioned as self-understanding, not therapy.

Beyond the consumer app, I built a full B2B layer: a marketing and onboarding funnel with quiz-driven onboarding (in the spirit of Headway's flow), and an enterprise admin dashboard showing team-level emotional trends, concerns, and AI-generated suggestions for improving team wellbeing - built with privacy safeguards so individual responses stay protected.
App design was heavily shaped by Skillsta's patterns. Built and shipped solo across the consumer app, marketing site, onboarding, and B2B product.

sections.title: From quiz to a personalized emotional journey
sections.intro: The product is structured to take a cold visitor from a generic landing page to a journey that feels tailored to what they're actually struggling with.

steps.title: Quiz-driven onboarding
steps.description: Consumer landing page onboarding gathers context through a short quiz flow, similar in spirit to Headway's onboarding, to understand what the user is dealing with before they land inside the app.

steps.title: Guided journeys and Moments
steps.description: Users choose a journey and move through interactive Moments combining insight, reflection, journaling, and choice-making, working with their internal 'parts' rather than generic advice.

steps.title: Personalized insight and daily rituals
steps.description: After each Moment, the user gets a tailored insight based on their answers and history. Daily notes and an activity tracker bring users back to revisit key Moments and reinforce growth over time.

media.alt: Partly insight and daily ritual screen

items.title: Separate enterprise platform
items.decision: Built distinct onboarding/landing experiences and a dedicated admin dashboard for enterprise customers.
items.rationale: Enterprise buyers need team-level, privacy-safe analytics and improvement suggestions, a fundamentally different job than an individual's personal reflective journey.

items.title: IFS as the structuring framework for content
items.decision: Built all lesson content around the Internal Family Systems model instead of generic CBT-style or mindfulness content.
items.rationale: Gave the app a distinctive, coherent narrative frame and a clear positioning wedge against mass-market wellness apps built on generic content.

items.title: Quiz-based onboarding modeled on Headway
items.decision: Adopted a quiz-driven onboarding flow to personalize the user's entry point into the app.
items.rationale: A proven conversion pattern in wellness/EdTech that lets the app learn through the very first steps of user interactions and provide a much more personalized experience.

sections.title: How Partly was built
sections.intro: A React Native app backed by PostreSQL and Supabase for internals, with a separate Next.js layer covering consumer marketing, quiz onboarding, and the B2B landing page and admin dashboard.

items.title: Architecture
items.description: Typescript all around. React Native/Expo consumer app; Next.js marketing/onboarding site plus a separate B2B landing page and admin dashboard; PostgreSQL + Supabase backend shared across all surfaces.

items.title: Data and state
items.description: PostgreSQL-backed vector embeddings used to retain conversational and journey context across sessions. The B2B dashboard ran team-level aggregation logic that anonymized individual responses before surfacing trends, concerns, and improvement suggestions to admins.

items.title: Quality and delivery
items.description: Shipped a full curriculum of 75+ interactive lessons across three journeys, plus a working B2B analytics product with its own free-trial onboarding funnel for enterprise teams, separate from the consumer signup path.

outcomes: Shipped a full IFS-based curriculum (75+ lessons across three journeys) alongside a working B2B analytics product.
Learned that positioning matters as much as content depth for wellness/EdTech products: communicating 'not therapy' clearly while still feeling credible and useful was an ongoing challenge.
Built an end-to-end product containing content systems, AI personalization, mobile UX, and B2B analytics, balancing between experimentation and technical execution.

projects.name: Plurabook
projects.summary: An AI-powered mobile app for creating, discovering, and reading personalized books. Users can turn a genre, idea, or a few lines of text into a complete story, then save and download books for offline reading.

overview.title: Making book creation accessible
paragraphs: Writing a book traditionally requires a significant amount of time, skill, and commitment before an idea becomes something readable. Plurabook explored how AI could reduce that barrier by letting anyone start with a genre, an idea, or just a few lines and turn it into a complete book.

As the solo founder and product engineer, I owned the product end-to-end, from product concept and UX through mobile development, backend architecture, AI integration, and release. The experience combined AI-assisted creation with a familiar reading model: users could create books, explore stories by genre, build a personal bookshelf, and download books for offline reading.

sections.title: From an idea to a readable book
sections.intro: The main journey takes a user from a simple creative idea to a finished book they can read, save, and return to later.

steps.title: Start with an idea
steps.description: Users choose a genre and provide a story idea, premise, or a few lines of text. The interface keeps the starting point lightweight so users can begin creating without needing to outline or write an entire story themselves.

steps.title: Generate the book
steps.description: Plurabook transforms the user's input into a structured story. The generation flow abstracts away the complexity of AI content creation and presents the result as a complete book rather than a raw AI response.

steps.title: Read and save
steps.description: Once created, the book becomes part of the user's personal library. Users can read it in-app, save it to their bookshelf, and download it for offline access.

sections.title: Reducing the friction between ideas and stories

items.title: Start with almost nothing
items.decision: Allow users to begin with a genre, a rough idea, or only a few lines of text.
items.rationale: The goal was to remove the blank-page problem. Users shouldn't need to understand story structure or know exactly what they want to write before they can start.

items.title: Make AI feel like a product
items.decision: Present generation as part of a structured book-creation experience rather than exposing users directly to an AI chat interface.
items.rationale: The value is the finished story, not the underlying model. A focused creation flow makes the technology easier to understand and gives the generated content a clear purpose.

items.title: Treat generated books like real books
items.decision: Build around familiar reading concepts such as a bookshelf, genres, saved books, and offline reading.
items.rationale: Users already understand how libraries and reading apps work. Using familiar mental models makes an AI-generated book feel like a piece of content they own and can return to, rather than a temporary AI interaction.

sections.title: Building an AI-native reading experience
sections.intro: Plurabook combined a mobile reading experience with AI-powered content generation, requiring the product architecture to handle both conventional application state and longer-running generation workflows.

items.title: Architecture
items.description: Built the mobile application with React Native and TypeScript, with Supabase providing the backend layer. The architecture separated the core reading, bookshelf, discovery, and book-generation flows while keeping the system lightweight enough to iterate on as a solo engineer.

items.title: AI and data
items.description: Integrated AI generation into the book creation flow and designed persistent data around users, books, genres, reading state, saved content, and generated stories. The AI layer was treated as a product capability rather than a standalone chat feature.

items.title: Offline reading
items.description: Implemented the ability to download books for offline reading, requiring the app to distinguish between remotely available content and locally persisted books while maintaining a consistent reading experience.

outcomes: Designed, built, and published an end-to-end AI-powered mobile product independently, covering product strategy, UX, mobile engineering, backend integration, AI generation, and release.
Explored how AI can reduce the barrier to creating long-form content by turning lightweight prompts into structured, readable books.

The project highlighted a key product challenge: generating books is technically achievable, but creating a reading format that users consistently choose over faster forms of entertainment requires stronger validation and iteration.

projects.name: Syrnyk
projects.summary: An AI-powered cooking companion that turns whatever's in your fridge into ready-to-cook recipes, snap a photo, get a personalized recipe with full macro/micro breakdowns and a guided, step-by-step cook mode.

overview.title: Cook from what you already have
paragraphs: Most recipe apps assume you're starting from a shopping list. Syrnyk starts from your fridge, snap a photo of your groceries and the app recognizes what you have, then generates recipes built entirely around it, tuned to skill level, available appliances, food type, and time constraints.

Every recipe comes with a full nutrition table, ingredient-by-ingredient guidance, and a guided cook mode with per-step timers and instructions, so users go from 'what do I even make' to plated food without leaving the app.
Built and shipped solo end to end: product, design, mobile app, backend, and a fully automated content pipeline that published SEO-oriented recipe posts daily to drive organic acquisition.

sections.title: From fridge photo to finished plate
sections.intro: The whole product is built around collapsing the distance between 'I have random ingredients' and 'I'm confidently cooking something with them.'

steps.title: Track your fridge
steps.description: Snap a photo of your groceries or fridge and AI recognizes each item automatically, or add items manually for full control. This becomes the live inventory recipes are generated from.

steps.title: Generate a personalized recipe
steps.description: Set skill level, available appliances, food type, cuisine, occasion, and time constraints, Syrnyk generates a recipe from what's actually on hand, or produces a random recipe if you'd rather be surprised.

steps.title: Cook, guided, step by step
steps.description: Each recipe breaks down into steps with the specific ingredients needed at that step, built-in timers, and a full macro/micro nutrition table. Finished recipes save to a filterable Cookbook and cooking History for reuse and inspiration.

items.title: Photo-based fridge scanning over manual-only entry
items.decision: Built the first of it's kind on the market AI ingredient recognition from a fridge/grocery photo, with manual entry as a fallback for full control.
items.rationale: Typing in every ingredient is the single biggest friction point in any 'cook from what you have.

items.title: Fully automated AI content engine for SEO
items.decision: Built a separate pipeline that generated and published a new, SEO-oriented recipe post every day.
items.rationale: As a solo founder with no marketing budget or team, an automated content engine was the only scalable acquisition channel available.

items.title: Gamification and social layer on top of a utility core
items.decision: Added achievements, level-ups, and social profile elements alongside the core recipe-generation loop.
items.rationale: Recipe generation alone is a one-off utility action; the leveling and social mechanics were meant to convert single-use sessions into a recurring habit while feeding an organic content pipeline reaching millions of views of social media.

sections.title: How Syrnyk was built
sections.intro: A React Native app on a PostgreSQL + Node.js + Supabase backend, with two distinct AI systems doing different jobs: one recognizing ingredients and generating recipes for users, the other autonomously generating and publishing blog content.

items.title: Architecture
items.description: React Native/Expo mobile app talking to the backend. Two separate AI pipelines: an in-app pipeline for vision-based ingredient recognition and recipe/nutrition generation, and an independent automated pipeline that generated and published daily SEO recipe posts to a public blog.

items.title: Data and state
items.description: PostgreSQL held user fridge inventory, recipe history, cookbook entries, and achievement/level progress; Supabase Storage held user-uploaded fridge photos. Fridge inventory state fed directly into the recipe generation inputs.

items.title: Quality and delivery
items.description: Shipped as an iOS MVP via the App Store, with RevenueCat handling subscription/paywall logic. Iterated post-launch based on direct user and Product Hunt feedback (#7 launch week ranked), AI-generated nutrition facts, for example, were explicitly flagged as 'Beta' rather than presented as a professional estimate.

outcomes: Organic reach into the millions on TikTok, driven by recipre and cooking related content, with strong initial App Store pickup as a solo-built MVP.

Validated that the core AI loop: photo → recognized ingredients → generated nutrition-complete recipe, worked well as a product mechanic converting viral spikes into retained, paying users proved to be the harder problem.
Gained hands-on experience connecting viral acquisition, AI product mechanics, and retention, shaping how I approach product validation and growth.

projects.name: Nokeep
projects.status: Status unclear — public records conflict (one lists the entity as ceased, another as active)
projects.summary: A Belgian rental marketplace connecting renters with rental professionals and suppliers, letting people rent products and tools instead of buying them outright, for renters browsing and booking items, and for rental businesses gaining an online outlet.

overview.title: Own anything, temporarily
paragraphs: Nokeep was a two-sided rental marketplace: renters could search, browse, and book products and tools, then communicate directly with rental providers; rental businesses could create and manage listings, track inventory, and handle incoming rental requests.

I joined as Founding Frontend Engineer and led frontend architecture and technology decisions from an early stage, building custom design systems from the ground up. I also joined as a part of a product and marketing team, brainstorming and implementing multiple online and offline strategies.

sections.title: Listing an item for rent
sections.intro: The multi-step listing creation flow was one of the more complex pieces of the frontend, a rental business walks through several steps to get an item live and bookable on the marketplace.

steps.title: Start a listing
steps.description: A rental business begins a new listing from their inventory dashboard, entering the item into a guided, multi-step creation flow rather than a single long form.

steps.title: Fill in listing details step by step
steps.description: Each step of the flow (details, pricing/availability, photos, etc.) is backed by its own piece of Zustand state, kept deliberately separate from the API layer, so each step could be built, validated, and maintained independently.

steps.title: Publish and go live
steps.description: On submission, the accumulated Zustand state is passed through the API layer to create the listing, which becomes searchable and bookable by renters, with inventory and requests then manageable from the business's dashboard.

items.title: Separating UI, state, and API layers in the listing flow
items.decision: Structured the multi-step listing creation flow with a clear boundary between UI components, Zustand state management, and the API layer.
items.rationale: Gave each step of a genuinely complex flow clear state ownership, making individual steps easier to build, test, and maintain independently rather than as one tangled form.

items.title: Mixed rendering strategy in Next.js
items.decision: Used SSR for highly dynamic pages, ISR for public rental/listing pages where both SEO and freshness mattered, and SSG for static pages, combined with route/component-level code splitting and lazy loading for heavier functionality.
items.rationale: Kept SEO-critical marketplace content (listings) server-rendered and discoverable, while loading heavier interactive functionality progressively so it didn't block initial page performance.

items.title: Reusable UI/design-system patterns over page-specific builds
items.decision: Built custom, scalable UI systems and design patterns intended for reuse across the marketplace rather than one-off implementations per screen.
items.rationale: The marketplace had two structurally different user types (renters and rental businesses) sharing many of the same UI primitives, shared patterns kept the frontend consistent and easier to extend as the product grew.

sections.title: How the Nokeep frontend was built
sections.intro: Frontend architecture for a two-sided marketplace, built on Next.js/React/TypeScript with Zustand for state, designed to keep SEO-sensitive marketplace pages fast and server-rendered while the interactive parts stayed responsive.

items.title: Architecture
items.description: Next.js, React, and TypeScript frontend consuming REST APIs, structured around reusable UI/design-system components shared across the renter and rental-business sides of the marketplace.

items.title: Data and state
items.description: Zustand managed state for complex flows like multi-step listing creation, kept deliberately separate from both the UI layer and the API layer to give each step clear ownership of its own state.

items.title: Quality and delivery
items.description: Performance work centered on a mixed Next.js rendering strategy, plus route/component-level code splitting, lazy loading, CDN/image optimization, and caching of frequently accessed marketplace data.

outcomes: Led frontend architecture for a live, two-sided rental marketplace from an early stage, including its most complex flow (multi-step listing creation) and its core performance strategy.
Built shared, reusable UI design system rather than one-off screens, which held up as the marketplace expanded across renter and supplier-facing surfaces.

Was responsible for building main booking flows, including Airbnb-style booking calendars with availability statuses and booking systems, automated marketing campaigns for rental companies and post-production analytical and feedback loop work.
